Implication: Buyer financing and pricing can deteriorate as the certain income term shrinks. Renewal is not automatically landlord-controlled. Mitigation: Map option/notice dates; seek an extension and market bids before the financing window narrows.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Jack in the Box Inc. · FY2025 Form 10-K, SEC

Implication: SEC filings disclose franchise payment delays; the actual operator may be weaker than the brand. Mitigation: Verify obligor/guarantor, rent coverage, arrears and security; size a private carrying-cost reserve.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Jack in the Box Inc. · Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q, SEC

Implication: Closures can occur even while the overall chain survives; a profitable brand portfolio need not preserve every site. Mitigation: Obtain unit-level performance and reimage/commitment plans; assess alternative users before conceding rent.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Jack in the Box Inc. · Q3 FY2026 Form 10-Q, SEC

Implication: Wage floors and food/energy inflation can reduce a tenant’s ability to absorb rent increases. Mitigation: Underwrite normalized labor and food costs; avoid rent resets that make the location uneconomic.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: California Department of Industrial Relations

Implication: County population decline can restrain transaction growth despite nominal menu-price increases. Mitigation: Use flat/negative real-demand cases and verify actual catchment, not county averages alone.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: U.S. Census Bureau · QuickFacts

Implication: Information and film weakness can reduce nearby daytime demand even as healthcare grows. Mitigation: Diversify demand sources in site underwriting; do not capitalize one strong sector into the entire trade area.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: California Employment Development Department

Implication: Higher required yields can lower buyer bids independently of tenant performance. Mitigation: Stress exit pricing and discount rates; verify debt maturity and avoid forced-sale timing.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

Implication: Rent escalations below inflation erode real income; replacement costs can rise faster than NNN reimbursements. Mitigation: Compare real and nominal cash flows; negotiate appropriate bumps without impairing coverage.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics · Los Angeles area CPI

Implication: Roof, structure, parking, insurance gaps and unreimbursed administration can remain with the owner. Mitigation: Read the lease rather than the marketing label; commission a condition assessment and reserve study.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Jack in the Box Inc. · FY2025 Form 10-K, SEC

Implication: Vacancy can require carrying costs, tenant improvements, commissions and free rent before income resumes. Mitigation: Model zero-rent periods explicitly and obtain alternative-user bids before expiry.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Jack in the Box Inc. · FY2025 Form 10-K, SEC

Implication: A long fixed-rent extension can protect occupancy while surrendering upside or accepting weak credit. Mitigation: Compare extension value with current bids and market-rent reset alternatives; reject value-destructive terms.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: California Board of Equalization

Implication: A lease of 35 years or more including written options can constitute a change in ownership. Mitigation: Obtain property-tax counsel before executing an extension or restructuring options.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: California Board of Equalization

Implication: City ULA can materially reduce net proceeds above thresholds; it does not apply merely because a listing says Los Angeles. Mitigation: Confirm jurisdiction and closing-date rules; compare after-tax net proceeds, not asking price.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance

Metric: Tax leakage and failed exchange timing
Implication: Recapture, boot, state tax and missed exchange deadlines can reduce investable proceeds. Mitigation: Use private tax basis and a qualified intermediary before closing; evaluate a taxable diversified sale versus replacement-property risk.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Internal Revenue Service · 2025 Form 8824 instructions

Metric: Buyer retrading, financing failure and execution risk
Implication: Headline offers may not close; diligence can reveal defects and lenders can reprice. Mitigation: Require evidence of funds/financing, deposits and clear contingencies; maintain a fallback hold plan.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

Implication: Damage, access loss, customer displacement and smoke can interrupt rent even without building destruction. Mitigation: Check adopted hazard maps, hardening, insurance and rent-abatement clauses; stress prolonged outage.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: CAL FIRE · Palisades incident

Implication: Regional shaking can damage structures and roads/utilities; repair demand can raise costs. Mitigation: Obtain seismic/soil review, earthquake and rent-loss coverage quotes, and an engineered repair reserve.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: U.S. Geological Survey · UCERF3, Fact Sheet 2015–3009

Metric: Flood, debris flow and drainage failure
Implication: Effective flood mapping and post-fire debris pathways are site-specific; county location cannot resolve them. Mitigation: Review FIRM, local hydrology, elevation and exclusions; do not assume absence of a mapped zone means no risk.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: FEMA · Flood-map products and tools

Metric: Insurance nonrenewal, exclusions or slow recovery
Implication: Insurance proceeds may arrive late or exclude key perils; lender coverage requirements can force expensive replacement. Mitigation: Review full policies, limits and business-interruption periods; maintain liquidity rather than relying on disaster aid.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: California Department of Insurance

Implication: Lane reductions and pedestrian detours can hurt a drive-thru or walk-up location before transit benefits arrive. Mitigation: Check agency notices and driveway rights; do not pay for speculative transit uplift today.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority

Implication: A restaurant site may not permit the desired replacement use, density, parking or drive-thru. Mitigation: Verify zoning, overlays, legal nonconforming rights and entitlement cost before assigning residual land value.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning

Implication: Owner/operator liability can arise from current or historical contamination and delay transfer or financing. Mitigation: Obtain private Phase I/II work and legal allocation of obligations; no environmental clearance is asserted here.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Jack in the Box Inc. · FY2025 Form 10-K, SEC

Metric: Title, easement, parking or access defect
Implication: Encumbrances can invalidate assumed access, parking counts or redevelopment capacity. Mitigation: Review current title, survey, shared-parking agreements and condemnation records privately.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning

Metric: Pandemic, civil unrest or utility/cyber outage
Implication: Public-health restrictions, unrest or infrastructure failures can combine access loss with tenant cash-flow stress. Mitigation: Stress 12–24 months of interrupted rent plus carrying costs; review force majeure, abatement and security provisions.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Jack in the Box Inc. · FY2025 Form 10-K, SEC

Implication: Fuel and supply-chain shocks can affect ports, food costs and household spending at the same time. Mitigation: Use combined inflation-plus-low-demand scenarios; avoid treating sector indicators as independent guarantees.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: UCLA Anderson Forecast

Metric: Drought, extreme heat and water restrictions
Implication: Heat raises operating costs and can alter customer behavior; water constraints can affect landscaping and redevelopment. Mitigation: Review local utility rules, equipment efficiency and climate resilience; no numeric loss is inferred.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: California Office of the State Fire Marshal

Implication: One building, one tenant and one region can dominate personal wealth even when property cash flow is stable. Mitigation: Assess private net-worth concentration and cash needs; diversification may justify selling below a theoretical hold value.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Internal Revenue Service · 2025 Form 8824 instructions

Implication: Sale proceeds can be reinvested into an equally risky asset, held idle, or exposed to exchange deadlines. Mitigation: Compare after-tax diversified alternatives and fiduciary advice; an exchange is tax deferral, not automatic wealth creation.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Internal Revenue Service · 2025 Form 8824 instructions

Implication: Tourism and Olympics exposure can be temporary and unevenly distributed; construction costs occur before benefits. Mitigation: Underwrite recurring local demand first; assign no permanent event premium without site evidence.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Los Angeles Tourism & Convention Board

Implication: County statistics, old comparables and mismatched definitions can create false precision. Mitigation: Keep blank unknowns, retain source vintages, test assumptions and independently appraise the actual property.
Note: Qualitative decision analysis, not an official probability or loss estimate.
Source publisher: Caltrans · Long-Term Socio-Economic Forecasts
